{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded Day 1 visits with conflicting schedules",
      "quote": "Day 1 (Day 1) | Day 8 ±3 (Day 8) | Day 29 ±3 (Day 29) | Day 50 ±3 (Day 50) | Day 1 ±3 (Day 1) | Day 22 ±3 (Day 22) | Day 43 ±3 (Day 43) | Day 1 ±3 (Day 1) | Day 22 ±3 (Day 22) | Day 43 ±3 (Day 43) | Day 64 ±3 (Day 64)",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The schedule lists multiple visits labeled 'Day 1 ±3' (three times) and 'Day 22 ±3' (twice) and 'Day 43 ±3' (twice) without distinguishing cycle numbers, making it impossible to interpret the actual visit sequence and potentially causing scheduling errors.",
      "fix": "Rename visits with cycle numbers (e.g., Cycle 1 Day 1, Cycle 2 Day 1, etc.) and clarify the treatment cycles."
    },
    {
      "title": "High burden of vital signs at every visit including follow-ups",
      "quote": "Vital signs | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs are collected at every single visit, including EOT and Safety Follow-up, which adds burden for patients who are off treatment and may not need such frequent monitoring.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital signs at follow-up visits to only if clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Concomitant medications collected at every visit including survival follow-up",
      "quote": "Concomitant medications | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Concomitant medication data is collected at every visit, including survival follow-up, which is excessive and burdensome for patients in long-term follow-up.",
      "fix": "Limit concomitant medication collection to treatment visits and EOT; collect only targeted medications during follow-up."
    },
    {
      "title": "Hematology collected at every visit including survival follow-up",
      "quote": "Hematology | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Hematology labs are drawn at every visit, including survival follow-up, which is unnecessary and adds patient burden and cost.",
      "fix": "Remove hematology from survival follow-up; only collect if clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Blood chemistry collected at nearly every visit including follow-ups",
      "quote": "Blood chemistry | X | X |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Blood chemistry is collected at almost every visit, including EOT and Safety Follow-up, which is excessive for patients in follow-up.",
      "fix": "Reduce blood chemistry frequency during follow-up; consider only at EOT and if clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "CT scan and/or MRI at every tumor assessment and follow-up",
      "quote": "CT scan and/or MRI | X |  |  |  | X |  |  | X |  |  |  | X | X | X | X |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Imaging is performed at every tumor assessment and also at EOT and Safety Follow-up, which may be excessive and burdensome, especially for patients in survival follow-up.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing imaging frequency in follow-up to every 6 months or as clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "T cell immune monitoring PBMC sample collected at many visits",
      "quote": "T cell immune monitoring PBMC sample |  | X | X | X |  | X |  |  | X |  |  |  | X |  |  |",
      "page": 59,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PBMC samples are collected at multiple visits, which is burdensome for patients and requires significant processing; consider reducing frequency.",
      "fix": "Reduce PBMC collection to key timepoints (e.g., baseline, cycle 2, EOT)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs every hour during 4-hour observation after ISA101b",
      "quote": "Vital signs will also be taken every hour during the 4-hour observation period following ISA101b administration.",
      "page": 66,
      "section": "9.2.3.4 Vital Signs",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring vital signs every hour for 4 hours after ISA101b administration adds significant patient burden and staff time, especially on days with many other procedures.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing to every 30 minutes for first 2 hours, then hourly, or as clinically indicated."
    }
  ]
}
